Hippocampal reactivation of aversive experience promotes a slow-breathing recovery state
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02519-2Mahéo, Bagur et al. show that after escaping danger, mice enter a distinct slow-breathing state that promotes recovery from stress, revealing that recovery is an active physiological process rather than a passive return to baseline.

title: The identity gene Fezf2 is repurposed postnatally to specify inhibitory input in an activity-dependent manner
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02515-6Kroon et al. show that Fezf2, the gene that gives a cortical neuron its identity before birth, is reused postnatally under the control of neuronal activity to set how much inhibition that neuron receives.

title: Highly selective visual circuits in mouse frontal cortex
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02520-9The authors identify neurons in the frontal cortex of awake mice with highly selective visual receptive fields. These neurons prioritize encoding of binocular visual space, require V1 input and provide functional feedback throughout the visual cortex.

title: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02523-6Using fMRI data from speakers of 21 languages and multilingual language models, de Varda et al. show that brain encoding models trained on some languages predict responses to unseen languages, pointing to a shared meaning component across languages.

title: Presynaptic functional organization by phase separation
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02517-4This Review by Ogunmowo and Watanabe summarizes recent findings in the field showing how presynaptic functions are enabled, organized and coordinated by phase separation and discusses future directions in this branch of neuroscience.

title: Brain Predicts Spoken Mandarin Differently Than English
summary: Most neuroscience models of how we predict upcoming speech are based on English and European languages. Researchers recorded brain activity during a Mandarin audiobook, revealing that Mandarin listeners rely on tone-integrated sub-syllables rather than individual phonemes to anticipate speech.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, auditory cortex, auditory neuroscience, brain research, language, language processing, neurobiology, SfN

title: Adolescent Brain Circuits Shape Lifelong Social Drive
summary: Why are teenagers hard-wired to seek peer connection, and why do so many psychiatric disorders emerge during adolescence? Researchers found that disrupting a key prefrontal-to-striatum reward circuit during adolescence causes lasting social withdrawal in adulthood.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain development, brain research, developmental neuroscience, isolation, mental health, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, Ohio State University, social neuroscience

title: Why Nerve Pain Lingers
summary: Why can a light touch trigger intense discomfort long after a nerve injury heals? Researchers uncovered a Nono–Kcnq2 molecular pathway in the spinal cord that normally brakes pain-neuron firing, and showed that restoring it relieves neuropathic pain.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, Pain, brain research, nerve pain, neurobiology, neuropathy, pain, spinal cord

title: Rising Blood Sugar in Young Adults Hurts Midlife Brain Health
summary: Gradually rising blood sugar starting in your 20s can quietly erode cognitive performance decades before old age. A 30-year study found that young adults with creeping glucose levels scored worse on midlife memory and executive function tests, even without developing Type 2 diabetes.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, Aging, AHA, brain research, cognition, glucose, glucose. metabolism, metabolism, neurobiology

title: Psilocybin and Ketamine Break Rigid Habits to Improve Decision-Making
summary: How do psychedelics help the brain break free from entrenched patterns of thought? A new study shows that both psilocybin and ketamine reduce reliance on repetitive habits and sharpen sensory-guided decision-making by gently sculpting orbitofrontal cortex activity.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, Boston College, brain research, decision making, ketamine, neurobiology, psilocybin, psychedelics, psychopharmacology

title: The Brain Creates Body Ownership Before Touch Occurs
summary: How does your brain know your hand belongs to you? Mapping brain activity every four milliseconds during the rubber hand illusion, researchers discovered that body ownership unfolds in three rapid phases, starting even before physical touch occurs.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, bodily sensations, brain research, Karolinska Institute, neurobiology, tactile perception, touch

title: Scientists Build 6,986 Digital Brain Twins to Study Dementia
summary: Every human brain ages within a unique biological and social context. An international team created 6,986 personalized biophysical "digital brain twins" across 16 countries, turning fMRI scans into virtual laboratories to decode how aging, dementia, and environmental exposures alter neural dynamics.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Aging, AI, Artificial Intelligence, brain aging, brain research, Deep Learning, dementia, Digital Twins, Machine Learning, neurobiology, Neurology, Neurotech, TCD

title: High-Speed Nanoscale Brain Imaging Uncovers Hidden Synapses
summary: Even the most detailed brain wiring maps often miss ultra-fine cellular connections. Researchers sped up 3D electron tomography 50-fold, uncovering hidden electrical synapses and tiny protrusions where neurons appear to "nibble" neighboring glia.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain mapping, brain research, Harvard, neurobiology, neuroimaging, synapses

title: Does Working Harder Make Learning Fun?
summary: Parents and teachers often tell kids that studying harder will make learning enjoyable, but psychology research suggests the opposite. A new study shows that effort boosts understanding, while genuine interest must come first to spark engagement.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, learning, neurobiology

title: Self-Objectification Alters Brain Response to Media
summary: How does the way a woman views her own body shape how her brain responds to sexualized images in the media? Researchers found that higher self-objectification is linked to dampened neural activity in aesthetic judgment regions.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, body image, brain research, neurobiology, Psychology, self obejectification, SfN

title: Brain Speech Hub Builds a “Blueprint” Before We Speak
summary: Textbooks have long taught that understanding speech and producing words happen in separate brain systems. A new study overturns that century-old model, revealing that a hub inside Wernicke's area builds an abstract "blueprint" for each word a quarter-second before we speak.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, language, left posterior superior temporal gyrus, lpSTG, neurobiology, UCSF, Wernicke's area

title: Air Pollution Reprograms Brain Immune Cells, Raises Dementia Risk by 25%
summary: How do microscopic soot and wildfire smoke particles injure the brain? Combining health records from 500,000 people with inhalation experiments, researchers foundPM2.5 air pollution raises dementia risk by 25% and reprograms brain immune cells.
